added_models.model: Applied BioMath QSP model of Aβ production, aggregation and antibody clearance

engagement.confidence_note: Full text read from Europe PMC (PMC8478725).
engagement.note: ODE model of Aβ and plaque, calibrated to clinical PK and amyloid PET for seven drugs including crenezumab.
engagement.quote: To understand why, we developed a quantitative systems pharmacology (QSP) model for seven therapeutics: aducanumab, crenezumab, solanezumab, bapineuzumab, elenbecestat, verubecestat, and semagacestat.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry at first use; the model was built after crenezumab's PET results were public.

engagement.magnitude_basis: simulated plaque change (<5% fall at 200 weeks) vs BLAZE florbetapir SUVR (no significant change)
engagement.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC8478725); the patient side, BLAZE (NCT01397578, no registry results), is read at abstract level; model_src carries the patient source here because the source itself states the comparison.
engagement.note: Model reproduced crenezumab's near-absent plaque fall, attributing it to IgG4's weak phagocytic clearance; BLAZE PET had shown no fall in 2018.
engagement.short: QSP reproduces crenezumab's flat amyloid PET
engagement.quote: Crenezumab and solanezumab were predicted to have < 5% plaque decrease from baseline after 200 weeks of treatment.
engagement.reason: Calibrated after BLAZE; reproduces flat PET
engagement.judgement: Retrodiction: the model was calibrated to observed PET data including crenezumab's (Salloway 2018 BLAZE: florbetapir primary not met), so 'retro', not 'same'. The paper says only aducanumab's 1-3 mg/kg titration was predicted a priori; aducanumab is not a member.

added_models.model: In-vitro binding to Aβ monomers, protofibrils and fibrils (inhibition ELISA, immunodepletion, SPR)

efficacy.population: Early AD (MCI or mild dementia), amyloid-positive
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read from Europe PMC (PMC10119362).
efficacy.note: Lecanemab's binding profile across Aβ species measured side by side with other antibodies.
efficacy.quote: We have characterized the binding properties of lecanemab, aducanumab, and gantenerumab to different Aβ species with inhibition ELISA, immunodepletion, and surface plasmon resonance.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry at first use of this assay panel; run after Study 201's 18-month results were public.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: tenfold protofibril-over-fibril selectivity vs clinical benefit and lower ARIA-E than fibril binders
efficacy.population: Early AD (MCI or mild dementia), amyloid-positive
efficacy.confidence_note: Sponsor (BioArctic) authors; the comparison is hedged ('may explain') and contrasts lecanemab with non-member antibodies. Full text read (PMC10119362).
efficacy.note: Tenfold protofibril selectivity offered as the reason lecanemab worked and fibril binders did not; Study 201 results preceded it.
efficacy.quote: Lecanemab’s preferential and strong binding to Aβ protofibrils may explain the difference in clinical efficacy and lower ARIA-E frequency as compared to aducanumab and gantenerumab.
efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction: epub 17 Oct 2022, after Study 201 (Swanson 2021) and Clarity AD's topline; the comparator antibodies are outside the member list, so only lecanemab's own efficacy is scored. model_kind ex_vivo is the nearest enum value for a cell-free in-vitro binding assay.

added_models.model: Antibody binding to CAA Aβ fibrils isolated from human leptomeningeal tissue

safety.population: AD trial populations of each antibody (crenezumab, lecanemab and non-members)
safety.note: Binding of therapeutic antibodies to CAA fibrils from human leptomeninges measured to relate to ARIA-E.
safety.short: Human CAA fibril binding assay run
safety.quote: We investigated therapeutic Aβ antibody binding to cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA) fibrils isolated from human leptomeningeal tissue to study whether this related to the ARIA-E frequencies previously reported by clinical trials.
safety.judgement: Opening entry at first use; every ARIA-E rate it is compared with was already published.

safety.magnitude_basis: rank of CAA fibril binding vs rank of ARIA-E frequency (crenezumab ~0%, lecanemab 12.6%, fibril binders 25-35%)
safety.population: AD trial populations of each antibody (crenezumab, lecanemab and non-members)
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PubMed; PMC11091209 not read). Sponsor (BioArctic) authors.
safety.note: Negligible CAA binding for crenezumab and low binding for lecanemab matched their low ARIA-E rates against high-binding antibodies.
safety.quote: Lecanemab showed a low binding to CAA fibrils, consistent with its relatively low ARIA-E frequency of 12.6%, while aducanumab, bapineuzumab, and gantenerumab all showed higher binding to CAA fibrils and substantially higher ARIA-E frequencies (25-35%).
safety.reason: Reproduces ARIA-E rank order post hoc
safety.judgement: Retrodiction (Clarity AD ARIA-E 12.6% published 2022). Scored as reproducing the human ranking; it does not predict lecanemab's absolute ARIA-E excess over placebo.

added_models.model: Tg2576 mice given mAb158, lecanemab's murine version

safety.model_filed: BLA 761269 pharmacology review: Tg2576 studies W-20090278 and W-20100295 with mAb158
safety.population: Early AD (MCI or mild dementia), amyloid-positive
safety.confidence_note: First-use year inferred from study codes in the FDA pharmacology review.
safety.note: mAb158 dosed to aged Tg2576 mice; microhemorrhage later assessed by H&E and Berlin blue histology.
safety.quote: Microhemorrhage studies were conducted in mice dosed with mAb158 based on the concern for lecanemab-induced cerebral hemorrhage.
safety.judgement: Opening entry; 2009 is the study-number year (W-2009xxxx), a proxy for first use.

safety.model_filed: BLA 761269 pharmacology review: no microhemorrhage or hemosiderin in Tg2576 mice given mAb158 up to 50 mg/kg weekly for 4 months
safety.magnitude_basis: mouse: no drug-related microhemorrhage vs Study 201 ARIA-H 6% drug vs 5% placebo
safety.population: Early AD (MCI or mild dementia), amyloid-positive
safety.confidence_note: FDA pharmacology review, summary review and label read in full from the source bundle.
safety.note: Mice showed no mAb158 microhemorrhage; Study 201 showed ARIA-H 6% on lecanemab vs 5% on placebo.
safety.short: No microbleeds in mice or Study 201
safety.quote: ARIA-H was observed in 6% (10/161) of patients treated with LEQEMBI compared with 5% (12/245) of patients on placebo.
safety.judgement: Pairing within the January 2023 FDA package: SumR states the mouse null (no mAb158-related microhemorrhage in Tg2576 or APPArcSwe); the label gives Study 201's ARIA-H. ARIA-E is not a histological readout in mice, so only microhemorrhage is scored.

safety.model_filed: BLA 761269 summary review: no mAb158-related microhemorrhage in Tg2576 or APPArcSwe mice
safety.magnitude_basis: mouse: no drug-related microhemorrhage vs Clarity AD ARIA-H 17% drug vs 9% placebo
safety.population: Early AD (MCI or mild dementia), amyloid-positive
safety.confidence_note: Patient side from the July 2023 label (Clarity AD, NCT03887455, no registry results posted); van Dyck 2022 full text not read.
safety.note: Clarity AD found ARIA-H in 17% on lecanemab vs 9% on placebo; the mice had shown none.
safety.quote: ARIA-H was observed in 17% (152/898) of patients treated with LEQEMBI compared with 9% (80/897) of patients on placebo.
safety.reason: Mouse silent; Clarity AD doubled ARIA-H
safety.judgement: Microhemorrhage is a harm mice can show (intact 2H6 caused it), so the model's silence is contradicted. The label adds there was no increase in isolated ARIA-H, so the excess travels with ARIA-E, which mice cannot show; scored contra at medium confidence. magnitude null: model null vs a ~2x patient excess.

considered_not_added: tg-ArcSwe + mAb158 microhemorrhage (checker 'missing' item): already a tracked model_id in the draft; the safety contra belongs in the main draft, not a parallel track. The Tg2576 half of the same FDA statement is added here as tg2576-mab158.

Tg2576 + mAb158 engagement (plaque unchanged at 4 months in the FDA PharmR, but cut at 18 weeks/35 mg/kg in Rizoska 2024): not added; it duplicates the draft's tg-ArcSwe engagement call, which hangs on an open checker rule question (protofibrils never measured in patients), and the two Tg2576 results disagree with each other.

Lecanemab sponsor popPK/PD and exposure-response models (ClinPharmR, Study 201): fitted to the same patients they describe; no out-of-sample prediction compared with a later trial was found in the review. The 2025 maintenance-dose and subcutaneous approvals relied on modeling, but their sources were not read within budget.

Crenezumab exposure-response modeling behind the 60 mg/kg CREAD dose: patient-derived, and no model paper with a stated prediction was found (search returned only the CREAD results paper and the PK/PD paper, whose abstract could not be retrieved).
Ponezumab plasma Aβ 'peripheral sink' PK/PD model: no model-vs-patient comparison found.
Clausznitzer 2018 QSP model (cited by Madrasi as capturing crenezumab PK/PD): not read; no comparison verified.

Söderberg 2024 lecanemab binding to protofibrils isolated from AD brain (PMID 38906341): abstract not retrieved (rate limit); same binding-assay lineage as abeta-species-binding-invitro, no separate patient comparison verified.
ACU193 vs lecanemab ex-vivo mouse brain binding (2026) and B28 APP knock-in mice (2026): no patient comparison.
Human genetic (APP A673T protective variant) and PSEN1 E280A kindred (API Colombia): the first bears on Aβ production (BACE tile); the second is a patient population tested in a trial, not a model.
Patient-derived cells, organoids or ex-vivo drug sensitivity for anti-Aβ antibodies: none found.

gaps.lead: safety, lecanemab, contra (tg-arcswe-mab158 plus Tg2576 with mAb158), year 2023: SumR no mAb158 microhemorrhage vs Clarity AD excess ARIA-H
gaps.detail: tg2576-mab158, safety: 2009 untested opening, 2023 same (Study 201 ARIA-H 6% vs 5%, Jan 2023 label), 2023 contra (Clarity AD ARIA-H 17% vs 9%, Jul 2023 label); the SumR line cited covers the APPArcSwe half too, so no parallel tg-arcswe-mab158 safety track is added

gaps.lead: efficacy, lecanemab: Study 201 missed its 12-month Bayesian ADCOMS gate (64% vs 80%) before Clarity AD met its primary in 2022
gaps.detail: Changes nothing scored: check.json adjudicates efficacy entry 3 (tg-arcswe-mab158, 2022) to untested (rules 4 and 8; the mouse behavioural null was not relied on and the model stated no benefit prediction on a clinical endpoint), so the track has no benefit prediction for Study 201's missed 12-month Bayesian ADCOMS gate (Swanson 2021, doi 10.1186/s13195-021-00813-8) to be scored against; draft entry 3 judgement already records the 201 miss.
